classes.blurb: You came out on the last tide to bury somebody, and you were still on the flat when the bell said two. The staff is the one you walked the causeway with and the lantern is the one you carried for the coffin; neither was ever meant to be a weapon and both are what you have. You are the balanced hand — nothing on this rock is easy for you and nothing on it is impossible.
classes.name: Mourner

classes.blurb: You worked the rock. You met the boats at the causeway head, you carried the dead up off the flat, and you cut the ground they went into. On the night of the Long Tide you were out there doing the job when the toll came, and you turned round with everybody else. Heavy work made a heavy hand: the shovel-blade swings slow and lands like the rock it cut, and the door-shield came off a priory door that is still standing.
classes.name: Sexton

classes.blurb: You pulled an oar for Odo Ferrier, thirty years of the dead going out and the fee coming back. You were in the boat on the night of the Long Tide, four at a time, until it went over with a full load. The gaff has the reach a boat-hook needs and the knife is for line, not for men, and you are quick because nobody slow ever kept that seat.
classes.name: Ferrier's Mate

classes.blurb: You came out about the crack in Mercy. You had a fee agreed, a hammer for sounding a bell rather than for breaking one, and a coil of line to hang a plumb from the crown — and you were still on the flat with your tools in your fist when the wrong number rang. You are the only one who came up this tide already knowing how the thing above you is put together.
classes.name: Bellwright
